chunks: What al-Shaykh—may Allah, Exalted is He, support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Miskān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“If a small thing falls into the well and dies in it, then draw from it buckets.” He said: “If a junub falls into it, then draw from it seven buckets. If a camel dies in it, or wine is poured into it, then all the water must be drawn out.”

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَاءُ كُلُّهُ: all of the water, indicating complete removal in severe contamination
key_terms.بَعِيرٌ: a camel, whose death in the well necessitates drawing out all the water
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state requiring ghusl due to major ritual impurity
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: wine, an impure substance that contaminates the well
key_terms.سَبْعَ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets, the specified amount to be drawn in one case
key_terms.فَانْزَحْ: draw out water from the well as a means of purification

ai.seo_question: What should be done if an impurity falls into a well according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the purification of well water when it is contaminated by different impurities. It distinguishes between lesser and greater causes of contamination, specifying different amounts of water to be removed depending on what has fallen into the well.
